newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: NTT to get S.Lanka Telecom stake - sources.
newsitem.headline: NTT to get S.Lanka Telecom stake - sources.

text.p: Japan's Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Company (NTT) will be awarded a 35 percent stake and management of the state-owned Sri Lanka Telecom, industry sources said on Thursday.
They said NTT would pay $225 million for the stake and management of Sri Lanka Telecom, which has a monopoly of international lines into the Indian Ocean island.
The deal was expected to be announced in early August, they told Reuters.
NTT was one of six companies who bid for the stake, which the Sri Lankan government is selling as part of its privatisation programme.
Government official have said restructuring Sri Lanka Telecom tops the country's list of reforms needed to improve its creaking infrastructure and is essential to encourage foreign investment.
NTT and France Telecom were both shortlisted for the final round of bidding.
The industry sources said NTT was likely to retain Telecom's 8,300 workforce and would have three seats on the company's board to the government's five.
The chief executive of the company would be appointed by NTT, they said.
Officials at Sri Lanka Telecom were unavailable for immediate comment.
